sentence: This project builds a way to make HIV vaccine nanoparticles that carry well-folded envelope protein, using an enzyme to link it to ferritin.
This project builds proteins that join a cytokine to an antibody so it acts on chosen immune cells, and tests them in animal models.
This project builds an AI-powered system that joins genomic, spatial and clinical data and searches images to study cancer risk and tumor progression.
This project studies how the immune response in the intestines of preterm neonates leads to necrotizing enterocolitis and looks for ways to prevent it.
This project studies how rare damaging mutations in certain proteins in preeclamptic placentas change the way extravillous trophoblast cells develop and work.
This project studies the role of one type of voltage-gated ion channel in immune and neural functions during autoimmune injury of the central nervous system.
This project studies atrial fibrillation using several kinds of data to find risk factors that help choose patients who will benefit from invasive therapy.
This project builds a probe-based method to study active mucosal infection with Chlamydia trachomatis in humans and understand what drives protection and disease.
This project uses CRISPR genome editing to change the genetic composition of donor lungs so that transplant patients tolerate them better.
This project studies how cells move proteins and lipids inside and out, and how this movement builds and reshapes the extracellular matrix.
This project tests whether a drug that changes protein synthesis can treat salivary gland cancer, using human models of the disease.
This project studies how early life lead exposure links to cognitive function later in life, using baby teeth that older adults donated.
This project builds mice with human cortical interneurons grafted into specific brain regions to study how these neurons affect brain circuits and behavior.
This project tests whether a compound helps male and female mice survive whole body irradiation after exposure, and checks its levels in the blood.
This project builds a low-cost, portable confocal microscope that gives non-invasive, quantitative microscopic biomarkers of chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy.
This project tries to find out how genetic factors raise the risk of cardiac arrhythmias.
This project studies how bacterial cells make and break down diribonucleotides, how these molecules bind proteins, and how they affect bacterial growth and disease.
This project builds tools that separate molecules by their shape and interactions in controlled gas environments to study molecules in complex biological systems.
This project studies how a metabolic enzyme in tumor-infiltrating neutrophils works in metastatic breast cancer and tests whether blocking it improves response to immunotherapy.
This project studies how a gene that is often mutated in human tumors controls chaperone-mediated autophagy, a highly selective form of autophagy.
